Horrors At Funeral Parlours

By: Jane Lipman | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Tonight on Carte Blanche we talk to three families that have experienced traumatic service from funeral parlours

Summary:
Carte Blanche interviews 3 families that have experienced very bad customer service from three funeral parlours, Doves, Martin's and Avbob. Denzil Ulyate's mother, Glenis Lestrange (67) passed away on the 25th of May 2015, to be cremated on the 11th of June 2015. Adriaan Batt of Doves ,informed Denzil that his mother's body parts had been harvested by a syndicate.Minki Ngcobo, Chief Executive of Doves group, said that 6 funeral directors have been suspended, but Denzil says this is not true.Denzil has a phone recording and text messages of Adriaan Batt admitting guilt and offering Denzil a bribe. Denzil is happy to go on camera. Martin Venter in Carltonville, when his father-in-law passed away on the 13th of December 2015. The family made arrangements with Martins funeral parlour to have the body be fetched from the hospital and organise the cremation. On the 15th the family went to view the body and say their farewells. on the 17th they had the final funeral service. After the funeral the family was advised that the body will only be taken to the cremators on 4/01/2016. On the 28/12/2015, Martin's mother-in-law wanted to go say her final goodbye to her husband, when Martin called the funeral parlour to make arrangements, he was told that the body had been taken to the cremating services on the 17/12/2015. At about 10h30 Martin received an urgent call from his pastor urging him to rush to the funeral parlour alone, upon arrival, Martin discovered that his father-in-laws head was removed and he suspects it was Martins Funeral Parlour employees. Janet van Niekerk's mother died of natural causes and the family hired Avbob in Pietermaritzburg to help with the arrangement of the funeral. The day before the funeral, Janet and her family were shocked when they learnt that her mother's body had been taken to Port Sherpstone and allegedly cremated when a funeral had been arranged for Friday. Janet is distraught

Press Release:


Stolen Remains
A respectful burial facilitated by a professional funeral service can be a fitting tribute to a loved one. But even the dead are not safe from the hands of thieves. Syndicates are infiltrating funeral parlours to mutilate bodies and harvest organs, ostensibly for the lucrative muti trade. Are funeral parlours fuelling the illicit trade in human body parts? Carte Blanche investigates.


Script:


SCRIPT FUNERAL PARLOURS

Voice over : Dying and death is a deeply traumatic event for all of us at some point in our lives .All ancient cultures emphasised the proper burial of the dead. If burials were not done according to the rites it was seen as an insult to human value . We all want those closest to us to have a meaningful passage out of this mortal world . A violation of this right is something we don’t expect.
CLAIRE
WHEN A LOVED ONE PASSES THE GRIEF STRICKEN FAMILY ENTRUSTS FUNERAL PARLOURS TO TREAT THEIR DECEASED WITH DIGNITY AND RESPECT , WE HOWEVER HAVE COME ACROSS CASES WHERE BODIES HAVE EITHER GONE MISSING OR BODY PARTS HAVE BEEN HARVESTED WHILST IN THE CARE OF FUNERAL PARLOURS

DENZIL ULYATE had to nurse his mother through her final months before she died in Durban last May .
SOUND UP DENZIL She had pancreatic cancer , lymphatic leukaemia , lot of pain and she was on morphine, stuff like that . Riddled with cancer …It was an everyday fight just to keep going .I was at my mothers bedside for the last week of her life , and to see that life slip away , and deal with death , I never knew , I didn’t know , I didn’t think that I would be burying my mother as quickly as I did .Emotionally , it weighs on you heavily , very very heavily
For Denzil a respectful send off for his mother was profoundly important . Denzils family had always gone to Doves Funeral Services in Kwa Zulu Natal to bury all his family members. He was shocked when he got a call from Adrian Batt , the Doves Director responsible for the coastal offices ,saying that they had some bad news for him .
Denzil I got a call on the Monday afternoon from Mr Adrian Batt one of the Directors from Doves ,to say he’s got some bad news to tell me .


So Denzil arranged to meet with Adrian Batt and decided to record the conversation for his family records ,as Mr Batt said that his mothers body had been violated while at the funeral parlour .
Denzil sound up
RECORDING FROM ADRIAN BATT / show image of Adrian Batt
WHAT CAME BACK, WHAT I HEARD , FROM ONE OF THE DETECTIVES , WAS THIS WAS SOMEBODY WHO KNEW WHAT THEY WERE DOING

Introduce Naidoo here “Dr Steve Naidoo is one of the few specialist forensic pathologists in South Africa and was a state pathologist for over 20 years. He testified often in court “
SOUND UP NAIDOO “That in fact is a violation of the integrity of the body , of the dignity of that body, its also a violation of the human rights of people and their relatives …so certainly relatives and families have a right to feel violated and brutalised ,I certainly would feel the same if it was a family member of mine .
.
There was a syndicate that was taking body parts operating in the Durban Doves with the undertakers .
And MORE WIDELY, HUMAN BODY PARTS FROM ALL COMMUNITIES ARE BEING TRADED OUT OF FUNERAL PARLOURS FOR USE BY UNSCRUPULOUS FAKE TRADITIONAL HEALERS , SOME FETCHING UP TO TENS OF THOUSANDS OF RANDS PER BODY PART
VISUALS FROM THE MARKET HERE
Gogo Sheila Mbele Khama is a traditional health practitioner and believes that charlatan healers are using human body parts to enrich themselves fraudulently .
“I think from the African spirituality point of view its taboo or unethical or uncalled for , for anyone practising traditional healing and spirituality to use body parts .

In Carletonville , Rosaleen Landman found out about her husbands mutilated body at Martin’s funeral parlour last December . It had occurred over the Christmas holidays . Before his scheduled cremation, she had wanted to say her final goodbyes to her dead husband…
Sound up Rosaleen All I can think is that he was calling to me , to come and look at me, to come and see what they’ve done to me , that was what I think
The families pastor had to break the news to them . Martin Venter , Rosaleens son in law is still dealing with the aftermath .
Martin Venter sound up
So she said Martin please arrange for me so that I can view him as well , seeing that he’s here now , I want to say my final farewells , I’ll find out if it can be done .
The pastor told me that there was some sort of body mutilation that happened to my father in laws body , while he was lying there .He handed over to the co owner to explain what sort of mutilation it was , so obviously we are curious as to what had happened and he says his head had been removed . He cant say when it happened and how it happened…
You cant utter these words to your family ….especially telling your wife that your fathers head had been removed …it gone , you don’t know where it is.
It’s the most difficult thing I ever had to say to somebody .
QUESTION FROM CLAIRE ABOUT MARTINS
what happened from Martins side ?

They were remorseful , but they had no idea when this happened , how it happened, they had a suspicion though that its one of the current employees or an ex disgruntled employee .

Deon Koekemoer , General Manager at Martins claimed this has never happened before and says they are helping the police in their current investigation .
Firstly we were instructed not to really communicate with the family ,as we are seen as suspects as well .
From our side we have offered a 20,000 rand reward for information leading to the arrest and conviction of the perpetrator .


Sound up
I don’t think it a trend that has started , and has picked up, I think its always been there , there s a been a undercurrent , its in the cultural weave of certain societies

MTIMANDE NGWENYA is a traditional healer and a funeral parlour director …he agrees that sangomas are deeply spiritual
A real ….sangoma cannot use human body parts
He says in authentic traditional healing , the purpose is to heal the spirit and act as the connection between the living and the dead ancestors .

He says the FAKE healers give specific values to particular body parts harvested.
I am talking about hundreds of thousands of rands , anything not less than ten grands , I think it can be ten and two hundred thousand for that matter . It only depends as to the demand of the ritual that’s supposed to be performed. So for instance the breast of an albino , so these people are scarce , so they can arrange between fifty to hundred thousand .
Sound up SHEILA KHAMA
People are desperate , there are a lot of things that are going on in our country unemployment and other things that are causing people to become so desperate .
She says con artists posing as authentic traditional healers are exploiting destitute individuals .
We are shocked all of us as healers in South Africa , how that can happen and where is it coming from ?And we told ourselves that we will assist government at all costs to take this thing out of our space and root it out , because it has no space in traditional healing

The harvesting of body parts from the deceased is a criminal act , under the Human Tissues Act , and can be punished with substantial jail time of up to ten years .
Board Chairman of Doves, Khandani Msibi, says they took the case of Denzil Ulyate’s mother very seriously at Doves in Durban. He admitted some of his former employees stole human body parts.

“It is this organisation that has discovered what has happened ,and we did not hide it , we actually stopped operations where we could have proceeded with the cremations , we said we’re not proceeding with the cremation, so we're not proceeding with the cremation because something has gone wrong with our processes and we stopped the branch for five days and we reported the case to the police, we reported ourselves to the police that a crime has been committed in our premises and we took action against employees that have actually committed this crime, so anybody who is thinking about this matter can take comfort to the fact that Doves is a diligent in its processes and they will not hide failures that may happen within the processes".

But according to our funeral industry insider there were not adequate security measures in place

Sound up insider At the time of the incident for instance there was cameras but there cameras wasn’t working for a couple of months , there was no locks on the doors or on the fridges on the mortuary doors at all
But at night time there is a room for error .
Even though Doves say the security has been tightened, and that four employees were suspended after the incident , no arrests have been made due to insufficient evidence . Denzil Ulyate says Doves haven’t contacted him, and that they still have not given him an adequate explanation for what happened to his mother .
SOUND UP ADRIAN BATT , BUT THE REALITY WAS I DIDN’T CONTINUE BEING IN TOUCH WITH HIM NO , BUT FOR A FEW WEEKS AFTER THE EVENT , DEFINITELY I WAS IN TOUCH WITH HIM .

SOUND UP DENZIL Pretty much three months down the line , I received a couple of SMS’s from MR Batt which I have on file . NOTHING . Absolutely as if he’s just wanted us to go way , and nothings been said, this is just going to go away.
LINK FROM CLAIRE HERE IN FRONT OF LANDMAN HOUSE
The psychological damage to the Landman family who live here is deep ,they say they cannot find closure until their father is found and until the perpetrators are caught .
Sound up from Landman
I would to have the perpetrators caught and brought to justice . At this stage it already been two months and nothings happening , so we need , I need justice for my husband Hennie, somebody has to pay for what they have done ….




TWO FIFTEEN SECONDER AND ONE TEN SECONDER
ARE FUNERAL PARLOURS across the country FUELLING THE ILLICIT TRADE IN HUMAN BODY PARTS
WITH SOUND UP When I think of my mothers body ….

COMPLEX SYNDICATES TRADING IN HUMAN BODY PARTS ARE INFILTRATING PROFESSIONAL FUNERAL PARLOURS…

WITH SOUND UP

The desecration of a loved ones body in a funeral parlour is a crime , AND too traumatic to imagine …
